title: Le, la, je veux & -ion words
summary: English already contains lots of French. Here you learn je veux / tu veux (I want / you want), le and la (the), and how to use le/la for 'it' by putting it before the verb. English words ending in -ion are almost always the same in French, and they're all feminine (la).
points: Pause the track and answer out loud before the student does. Thinking it through slowly is how the method works.
je veux = I want, tu veux = you want. veux is related to 'volunteer' (someone who does something because they want to).
le (masculine) and la (feminine) = the. Every noun has a gender.
'It' is le or la too, and it goes before the verb: je le veux = I want it (literally 'I it want').
To ask a question, just raise your voice at the end: Tu le veux ?
-ion words (collection, tradition, opinion) are the same in French, all feminine, and you barely hear the final n.
le and la become l' before a vowel: l'opinion, l'organisation.
vocab: je le veux / je la veux
